subject: Dieux Skin

non_axis_bearing_units.reason: Exact-advertiser presence/absence capture contains no customer or product-experience unit to classify.

candidate_themes.label: Sensory and perceived product-integrity acceptability
candidate_themes.scope_change: Expanded the texture/finish/routine axis to include odor or scent acceptability and perceived product integrity, while forbidding contamination or prevalence inference.
candidate_themes.decision_effect: Odor can cause wash-off, return, rejection, nonrepurchase, or tolerance when performance is valued.
candidate_themes.rationale: The theme changes the same experience-and-routine fit decision as texture and finish; keeping it explicit inside that axis preserves mechanism without creating a quota-driven ninth axis.

candidate_themes.label: Reusable accessory use-cycle utility
candidate_themes.scope_change: Expanded packaging/dispensing usability to include reusable accessory adhesion, serum compatibility, cleaning, drying, storage, durability, repeated use, and waste reduction.
candidate_themes.decision_effect: The full use cycle determines whether reusable eye masks create repeatable utility or friction beyond nominal product performance.
candidate_themes.rationale: Container mechanics and reusable-accessory mechanics are distinct submechanisms of the same usability decision and are kept explicit in one axis.

candidate_themes.label: Availability and channel access
candidate_themes.scope_change: Expanded the service/fulfillment axis upstream to include stock, geography, retailer, and mail-forwarding access.
candidate_themes.decision_effect: A customer may defer, abandon, or reroute a purchase before product use when the product is unavailable in their channel or geography.
candidate_themes.rationale: Availability changes buying confidence and access, not product performance, so it belongs with the transaction/service axis.

candidate_themes.label: Additional named switching or comparison destinations
candidate_themes.decision_effect: Adds Dr. Jart, Lions Pose, Alpyn, and Kiehl’s as examples without changing the already-established switching decision.
candidate_themes.rationale: The source-native counterexample instantiates the existing repeat-purchase and switching axis; it changes no axis, mechanism, segment, claim ceiling, or competitive decision.

claim_boundary: The audit establishes admitted-corpus material-axis presence and route-bounded saturation only; it does not establish universal internet exhaustion or population prevalence.
